activity_context.topic_title: Conditions When a Determinant Equals Zero

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Determinant of a Matrix With Two Proportional Rows/Columns
examples.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14047809/assets/d95e60cbfa50178878e719166ace3dbff90c3cc5531acfc046d8354320cd4b00.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The matrix $A$ has proportional rows: 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14047809/assets/3f434912c97c20d04f703253fe41c169497cae82657cfbd0d8b548985549fe64.png)
As a result, $|A| = 0.$

- The matrix $B$ is a triangular matrix, so 

$$
|B| = (-1) \cdot 4 \cdot (-3) = 12 \neq 0.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has a zero row: 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14047809/assets/5f41ff4f7fe5aeae5865bef9ab16d5d97a3513277f70b797c4167882093ed079.png)
As a result, $|C| = 0.$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$

feedback.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{5} & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}4 & \sqrt{3} & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}|
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The matrix $A$ has a zero column: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 1 \\ \sqrt{5} & 0 & 4 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|A|=0.$

- Since $B$ is a diagonal matrix, we obtain 

$$
|B|=3\cdot (-1)\cdot 5=-15\ne 0.
$$

- The matrix $C$ has identical columns: 

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}4 & \sqrt{3} & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & \sqrt{5} & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|C|=0.$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|C|$ are equal to $0.$
